attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his essay, endorsed.

semantics.note: The sentence is a hyperbolic description of how LLMs feel to users ('completely', 'every single interaction'), offered to explain why people get attached. It is not a testable design specification. Treating it as an observation about design overstates what it commits him to.

contract.note: The verdict depends on reading 'affirming' as agreeing with or validating the user, and on treating hyperbole as a literal universal. Zitron supplied neither reading. In context, 'affirming' could mean attentive acknowledgment. One company's stated intent also cannot settle a generic claim about how LLMs are built.

evidence.note: Dated January 2026 constitution asks Claude to avoid sycophancy. It is a company statement of its own intent, not an independent finding about design or behaviour, and it covers one model.
Company says the constitution shapes training but admits outputs may not follow it. Self-description only.
2023 study finds sycophancy is a general tendency in RLHF models, which partly fits the claim's spirit. It is an earlier period and shows a tendency, not universal affirmation or design intent.

reviews.rationale: This is a rhetorical characterisation ('built to', 'every single interaction') in an essay about user psychology. Scoring it depends on an evaluator's reading of 'affirming'. The evidence cuts both ways: the sycophancy research fits the spirit, and one company's self-described anti-sycophancy aims cut against a literal design claim. Neither settles a hyperbolic generic, so it is not scored.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his essay, endorsed.

semantics.note: 'Absolutely cannot and will not do in the future' is a firm, categorical capability forecast. Taking the denied capabilities from the preceding paragraph (50% white-collar job elimination, superintelligence) is reasonable. The accusation about executives' motives is a separate, unscored point.

contract.note: Plain reading fixes the denied outcomes from the surrounding text, a fair and ordinary reading. The contract rightly says finite absence cannot support a claim with no deadline, and lets only a verified occurrence contradict it.

evidence.note: Payroll data through June 2026 show no economy-wide displacement, and a descriptive, non-causal gap for young workers. Far from the denied scale. Does not settle an indefinite forecast.
August 2026 benchmark shows current systems depend heavily on human guidance. Shows present limits, not a permanent ceiling.
September 2026 entry: a model solved 2 of 68 open Erdős problems. Narrow progress, not broad superintelligence.

reviews.rationale: Categorical 'will not' forecast with no deadline. Nothing in the packet shows LLM-caused job elimination at the referenced scale or broad superintelligence, so the early-resolution rule is not met. Their absence so far cannot confirm an open-ended 'never'. Unresolved.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his essay, endorsed.

semantics.note: Preserves the antecedent, both companies, both mechanisms, and 'as much as they can'. 'I think… will' is a plain expectation, not one of the policy's graded hedges, so it is treated as a forecast.

contract.note: Reading 'capacity limits' as serving capacity below demand is ordinary. Keeping the 'as much as they can' extent as a requirement is faithful to his words.

evidence.note: May 2026 report of Anthropic demand outpacing compute: evidence the condition was met. Restrictions it mentions are not dated after the post, and the same report describes limits being raised.
May 2026 OpenAI contributor confirms a regional capacity shortage (condition met). Says this is not rate limiting or degraded quality.
Anthropic's account of a quality regression around the post date, reverted April 20. Not tied to capacity, and the company says the cut was not deliberate (company disclosure).

reviews.rationale: The condition appears met for both companies. But the packet shows no attributable, deliberate cut in quality or allowances in response to capacity after April 14, and nothing on the maximal extent. No deadline was stated and no completed episode meets the early-resolution rule. Unresolved.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his essay, endorsed.

semantics.note: 'I see no scenario' is emphatic, unhedged exclusion, equivalent to 'won't'. The context sets scope to Anthropic and OpenAI. Phrasing it as his mental state is acceptable, since the contract scores the forecast.

contract.note: He excluded both lower costs and eased rate limits, so an implemented same-plan rate-limit increase is a fair, ordinary counterexample. The ambiguity in 'costs' does not affect the result.

evidence.note: Dated May 6, 2026 provider announcement, effective that day, doubles Claude Code five-hour rate limits on existing plans and removes the peak-hour reduction. The contract names this source type as acceptable.

reviews.rationale: Under the contract, any implemented easing of rate limits on an existing plan by either company after April 14 is decisive. Anthropic's May 6, 2026 change doubled recurring five-hour limits on existing plans, effective immediately. That is a recurring change, not a one-off reset or a new tier, so the forecast that rate limits would not be eased is contradicted.
